acceptance: Linux test jobs finish with at least 30% headroom below their timeout on main.
The Windows job's actual test coverage is confirmed and documented.
context:
2026-11-17:
- The re-run of test (py3.13) on #93 was cancelled again at 35m. GitHub kept no log for the cancelled job (BlobNotFound).
- The Windows job runs only tests/unit/test_bootstrap.py plus an isolated bootstrap smoke, which explains its 0m.
- The owner chose to diagnose before merging the release. PR #94 adds pytest-timeout and runs CI with --timeout=300 --durations=25, and raises the Linux job limit to 45m.
- Making the suite itself faster remains open under this item.
description:
On 2026-11-17 the release PR #93 (v0.2.14, metadata-only diff) hit the 30-minute job limit in `test (py3.13)` (run 44165674647, job 134330933901). It was cancelled inside `uv run -- pytest`. Recent main runs show the Linux test jobs at the edge of that limit:
- aa4dd538: py3.13 28m, py3.11 27m
- 9ca458b1: 24m, 21m
- 03f6b1f7: 28m, 25m

The suite grows with each feature (5302 tests at v0.2.14), so timeouts will become routine and block merges.

The Windows py3.12 job reports 0m. Check what it actually runs.

Options: profile the slowest tests (`--durations`), parallelise with pytest-xdist if the suite is safe for it, split into shards, or raise timeout-minutes with a recorded budget. Prefer making the suite faster over raising the limit.
